what: every live number of Mare Liberum, the open sea for agents, in public
rule: Aggregated counts only: no address and nothing about a person. The sea's own calls are counted nowhere and crawlers never as agents. Measured and modelled numbers stay apart; zero stays zero, and a day without a record says so (recorded: false) instead of 0.

work.what: A working session is a caller on one UTC day with at least one real action: a tool called at an MCP door (/mcp or /mcp/app), a message with a task to the A2A door, or a task brought to ask, decide, the brain or the doors over HTTP.
work.never: Never counted: the sea's own calls, crawlers, people in a browser, registries and monitors that only connect and list the tools, and Angel, the house agent.
work.how: A caller is told apart by its network (an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64) and the family of its client, salted with a secret the node never writes down and kept in memory for the day only; at most 3 working sessions count for one network a day. A session id a client sends is not trusted (this node issues none at its MCP doors). Only the counts are written.
work.hosted: Hosted clients (claude.ai, ChatGPT and other apps) reach the sea from a few shared addresses under one program name, so many of their people fall into few sessions: for them the count is a floor.
work.caveat: Runs the operator schedules from an assistant (Claude at the app door every morning) may be counted until they carry the sea's own marker; nothing is guessed to take them out. A restart of the node during a day can count a caller twice that day.

mcp.note: tool calls at the open MCP door (/mcp, its other names and the event stream of 2024), counted per UTC day since the count began; the sea's own calls and crawlers are not counted; the app door (/mcp/app) is not counted here
